facts.text: Netos is situated within the flat terrain of the South Texas Plains, characterized by brushland vegetation like mesquite and prickly pear.
The area around Netos experiences a subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild winters that support a long growing season.
Netos faces a moderate flood risk due to its proximity to the Rio Grande and potential for heavy rainfall.
Subtropical woodlands near Netos support diverse wildlife, including white-tailed deer, the green jay, and the Texas tortoise.
Starr County, where Netos is located, was created in 1848 and named for James Harper Starr, a Republic of Texas official.
The economy of the region surrounding Netos historically revolved around vast cattle and sheep herds on family-owned ranches.
